userImpact: An employee opening /projects sees the list render fully and correctly, but the Health column shows a placeholder em-dash ('—') for every row instead of green/yellow/red health badges, and a single 403 is logged to the browser console. No crash, no broken layout, no blocked workflow — health badges are a manager-oriented decoration the employee role is not authorized to see anyway. Cosmetic + console noise only.
rootCause: FE/BE role-contract mismatch. The /projects route is gated ALL_ROLES (route-manifest.ts:300) and GET /api/projects (list) is gated ALL_AUTHENTICATED_ROLES which includes 'employee' (projects.controller.ts:374-375; role-presets.ts:67-75) → 200. But the batch health endpoint GET /api/projects/health is gated STAFFING_ROLES = project_manager/resource_manager/delivery_manager/director/admin (projects.controller.ts:343-344; role-presets.ts:48-54) which EXCLUDES 'employee' → 403. ProjectsPage fires fetchProjectHealthBatch unconditionally in a useEffect with no role guard (ProjectsPage.tsx:165-175), so an employee triggers the 403. The call degrades gracefully: fetchProjectHealthBatch swallows the rejection in a try/catch (project-health.ts:40-42) and resolves an empty Map; the Health column renders '—' via `healthMap.get(item.id) ?? null` (ProjectsPage.tsx:308-313) and all other consumers default (`?? 0`, `?? ''`). List rendering is unaffected.
suggestedFix: Gate the FE call behind staffing roles so employees never fire it. In ProjectsPage.tsx, compute `const canSeeHealth = hasAnyRole(principal?.roles, STAFFING-equivalent FE role constant)` (mirror route-manifest role helpers already imported at line 5) and early-return from the health useEffect (line 166) when false: `if (!canSeeHealth || state.visibleItems.length === 0) return;`. This is the lowest-blast-radius fix (1 file, ~2 lines), preserves the intentional BE gate, and eliminates both the wasted request and the console 403. Do NOT relax the endpoint to ALL_AUTHENTICATED_ROLES — health scores are a manager surface and the gate is deliberate (confirmed: resource_manager → 200, employee → 403). Optionally also hide the Health column header for non-staffing roles so the '—' placeholders don't appear.
pageState: /projects list renders fully for employee (HTTP 200 on list). Health column = '—' for all rows. Console shows one 'GET /api/projects/health 403 (Forbidden)'. No crash, no dead-end, no blocked action. Graceful degradation confirmed.
evidence: Live wire (deliverit-test-v2.agentic.uz, employee ethan.brooks@itco.local): GET /api/projects?page=1&pageSize=2 → HTTP 200; GET /api/projects/health?ids=... → HTTP 403 body {"error":"Forbidden","message":"Insufficient role for this operation.","statusCode":403}. Control (resource_manager sophia.kim@itco.local): GET /api/projects/health → HTTP 200. Source: src/modules/project-registry/presentation/projects.controller.ts:343-344 (@Get('health') @RequireRoles(...STAFFING_ROLES)); src/shared/auth/role-presets.ts:48-54 (STAFFING_ROLES has no 'employee') vs role-presets.ts:67-75 (ALL_AUTHENTICATED_ROLES has 'employee'); projects.controller.ts:374-375 (list = ALL_AUTHENTICATED_ROLES). FE caller: frontend/src/routes/projects/ProjectsPage.tsx:165-175 (unconditional health useEffect, no role guard); frontend/src/lib/api/project-health.ts:33-43 (try/catch swallows rejection, returns empty Map); ProjectsPage.tsx:308-313 (renders '—' when health absent). Route gating: frontend/src/app/route-manifest.ts:300 (/projects allowedRoles: ALL_ROLES).
